leads.title: UN Human Rights Committee - Toonen v Australia ruling
leads.documents: International ruling that Tasmania's criminalisation of private same-sex acts violated human rights; triggered federal action
leads.detail: Cited as UN Human Rights Committee ruling in favour of Nicholas Toonen on 31 March 1994, including quote on criminalisation not being reasonable/proportionate to prevent AIDS/HIV spread

leads.title: Human Rights (Sexual Conduct) Act 1994 (Cth)
leads.documents: Federal sexual privacy law legalising consenting adult sexual activity Australia-wide and prohibiting arbitrary interference in private
leads.detail: Cited as passed four months after UNHRC decision by Keating government; section 4 legalising sexual activity between consenting adults; Attorney-General Michael Lavarch quote

leads.title: High Court of Australia application - Toonen and Croome v Tasmania
leads.documents: Constitutional challenge seeking to invalidate Tasmania's anti-gay laws as overridden by federal 1994 Act
leads.detail: Cited as application on 14 November 1995 by Nick Toonen and Rodney Croome, argued pro bono by Alan Goldberg QC after legal aid denial

leads.title: Criminal Code Amendment Act 1997 (Tas)
leads.documents: Repeal of Tasmania's anti-homosexuality laws, decriminalising homosexuality
leads.detail: Cited as passed House of Assembly 26 March 1997, Legislative Council 1 May 1997 by one vote, Royal Assent 13 May 1997, effective next day; ended 21-year penalty regime

leads.title: Anti-Discrimination Act 1998 (Tas)
leads.documents: State anti-discrimination machinery prohibiting discrimination on gender, lawful sexual activity, sexual orientation, gender identity
leads.detail: Cited as outlawing discrimination and prohibited conduct with investigation/conciliation; amended September 2013 to extend to transgender and intersex people and offensive conduct

leads.title: Sex Discrimination Amendment (Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Intersex Status) Act 2013 (Cth)
leads.documents: Federal protection for LGBTI people in Tasmania on sexual orientation, gender identity and intersex status
leads.detail: Cited as federal law protecting LGBTI people in Tasmania alongside state Act

leads.title: Expungement of Historical Offences Act 2017 (Tas)
leads.documents: Scheme to expunge historic convictions for consensual homosexual activity and cross-dressing
leads.detail: Cited as introduced 6 April 2017 by Attorney-General Vanessa Goodwin, passed Assembly 2 May 2017, Council 21 Sept 2017, royal assent 21 Nov 2017, effective 9 April 2018; covers pre-1997 homosexual offences and pre-2001 cross-dressing under Police Offences Act 1935

leads.title: Tasmanian Anti-Discrimination Commissioner Report April 2015
leads.documents: Government report recommending establishment and modelling of historic homosexual conviction expungement scheme
leads.detail: Cited as April 2015 report leading to December 2015 Liberal Government announcement and June 2016 draft bill by Department of Justice

leads.title: Relationships Act 2003 (Tas)
leads.documents: State registered partnership scheme - significant and caring relationships - with near-marriage rights
leads.detail: Cited as effective 1 Jan 2004, first Australian registration open to all couples, amended 73 pieces of legislation; recognised federally as de facto from 1 July 2009; Sept 2010 recognition of out-of-state same-sex unions

leads.title: Births, Deaths and Marriages Registration Act 1999 amendments 2019 - gender-optional birth certificates
leads.documents: World-leading gender identity law removing surgery and divorce requirements, allowing self-declaration, non-binary/removal of gender, age 16 self-consent
leads.detail: Cited as Liberal bill Oct 2018 amended 20 Nov 2018 with Labor/Greens/Speaker Sue Hickey support, Council second reading 4 April 2019, Assembly approval 10 April 2019, royal assent 8 May 2019, relevant parts effective 5 Sept 2019; supported by Transforming Tasmania and Rodney Croome
